messages:
elena_s: FYI customer `acme-corp` opened a ticket — internal service DNS started returning NXDOMAIN after they migrated app VMs to a new VPC this morning. API 502s and healthchecks failing. Ticket #98712.

support_ian: Can you paste the failing fqdn? Also any quick dig outputs?

elena_s: fqdn is `svc.api.acme.internal`. From a repro VM in their new VPC: 
```
$ dig +short svc.api.acme.internal @169.254.169.253
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 12345
```
(169.254.169.253 is their DNS forwarder appliance IP)

ashok_m: Does that forwarder talk to Route53 Resolver endpoints or to an on-prem DNS? Any resolver rules in their account?

elena_s: They said they set up a Route53 Resolver outbound rule to forward `acme.internal` to partner cross-account Resolver endpoint in account 5555555555. We asked for `vpc-assoc` list and resolver rules — they provided screenshots showing the forwarding rule exists and has target IPs `10.10.2.4/10.10.2.5` (resolver endpoints in partner account).

oncall-luis: Can you run tcpdump on the VM while hitting dig? I suspect packets not reaching resolver.

elena_s: Ran tcpdump on the VM: 
```
sudo tcpdump -n -s0 -vv port 53
20:12:02.123456 IP 10.0.5.12.54823 > 10.10.2.4.53: 12345+ A? svc.api.acme.internal. (45)
20:12:02.123789 IP 10.10.2.4.53 > 10.0.5.12.54823: ICMP 10.10.2.4 udp port 53 unreachable, length 56
```
So UDP is getting ICMP unreachable.

ashok_m: ICMP port unreachable from 10.10.2.4 suggests something between the VM and the resolver is dropping/blackholing. Any egress allowlist / firewall / proxy in that VPC?

elena_s: They have an egress proxy appliance (managed by their infra team) that enforces allowlists. I asked for iptables/logs. They returned a snippet from the proxy logs: 
```
DENY udp 10.0.5.12:54823 -> 10.10.2.4:53 (rule: deny-dns-outbound)
DENY tcp 10.0.5.12:54823 -> 10.10.2.4:53 (rule: deny-dns-outbound)
```

support_ian: That explains NXDOMAIN — their DNS forwarder can't talk to the Route53 Resolver endpoint. Because the forwarding rule configured in their account relies on reaching that resolver IP, and the egress proxy blocks it.

oncall-luis: Two remediation options: 1) update egress policy to allow outbound TCP/UDP 53 to the resolver endpoint IPs (10.10.2.4/10.10.2.5) or 2) avoid cross-account forwarding by associating the private hosted zone directly with the VPC (if partner is willing) or create inbound resolver endpoints and conditional rules.

ashok_m: Also note UDP truncation -> TCP fallback symptoms can surface as failures if firewall allows UDP but blocks TCP 53 (common). Confirm both UDP and TCP 53 are allowed.

elena_s: Customer applied an allow rule for outbound 10.10.2.4/5 ports 53 UDP/TCP and retested. Dig now returns private A records: 
```
$ dig +short svc.api.acme.internal @169.254.169.253
10.2.7.21
```
And their API requests started succeeding.

support_ian: Great. For long-term, recommend they either: 
- Add explicit Resolver endpoint IPs to their egress allowlist (documented in the ticket), and ensure both UDP/TCP 53 allowed.
- Or change to VPC association model for the private hosted zone (no cross-account forwarding) if partner can add the VPC association — this avoids egress dependency.

ashok_m: Logged root cause as: egress allowlist on customer side blocking traffic to cross-account Route53 Resolver endpoint -> DNS forwarding failed -> NXDOMAIN and downstream API errors.

elena_s: Customer confirmed fix and will keep the egress rule. I updated the ticket with commands, tcpdump snippet, and recommendations. Closing after 24h stable. :white_check_mark: 

infra-bot: Deploy note: remind customers in onboarding doc to allow outbound 53 to resolver endpoints when using outbound forwarding to cross-account endpoints — created doc PR #412. :memo:
